$AVGO just cleared the bar, and the guide was the point.

Q1 FY2026:
• Revenue: $19.31B vs. $19.21B consensus – Beat by 0.5%
• EPS (Non-GAAP): $2.05 vs. $2.02 consensus – Beat by 1.5%
• Guide (next quarter revenue): $22.0B vs. $20.40B consensus – Above by 7.8%

Key takeaways:
• The AI engine is still accelerating. Management put Q1 AI revenue at $8.4B (+106% YoY) and guided Q2 AI semiconductor revenue to $10.7B. That is a step-up, not a glide path.
• This is not just “AI chips.” Broadcom is selling the whole rack-scale plumbing: custom accelerators plus AI networking. The networking attach is the durable part, it scales with every incremental XPU deployed.
• Margins stayed elite at scale. Adjusted EBITDA was $13.1B, 68% margin, and the company guided to 68% again in Q2. That tells you the operating model is holding even as AI mix grows.
• @VMware is behaving like a stabilizer, not a growth engine. Infrastructure software was basically flat YoY, which is fine, but it also means the upside is still overwhelmingly in semis and AI-related networking.
• Cash return posture is aggressive and consistent. $8.0B of free cash flow in the quarter, a new $10B buyback authorization, and continued heavy repurchases signal confidence in forward demand and margin durability.

Watch items:
• AI customer concentration and mix. The numbers are big, but the market is going to keep discounting anything that looks like a small set of hyperscalers controlling the slope.
• AI networking mix and content per cluster. Watch whether Broadcom continues to expand share of the scale-out fabric as 800G pushes toward 1.6T roadmaps.

After hours, the stock was choppy and last up about 0.5%. That reaction says expectations were already high, and investors are still debating how much of this AI wave is incremental versus timing and mix. The guide beats consensus decisively, but the tape is telling you the market wants proof the AI ramp can stay this steep without margin or concentration surprises.  

Bottom line: Broadcom is executing like a core AI infrastructure supplier, and the Q2 outlook reinforces that this cycle has more runway than the market is willing to price in tonight.
